chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

When the traveler cannot find water, let him seek it as long as he is within the time [for prayer]. But if he fears that the time will pass, let him perform Tayammum and pray at the end of the time. When he finds water, there is no repayment (Qada) upon him, and let him perform Wudu for what is next.

key_terms.قَضَاءَ: Repayment/Make-up (of a missed or performed prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who finds water after praying with Tayammum due to lack of time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ease in difficulty' (taysir) by prioritizing the preservation of prayer time over ritual perfection when water is scarce. It clarifies that the validity of the prayer is not contingent on the prior availability of water, but rather on the sincere effort to find it, ensuring the worshipper does not miss the obligatory time. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that Tayammum serves as a complete substitute for Wudu in the absence of water, maintaining the integrity of the prayer act.
